labels.cancelled_note: The run was cancelled by the user; only the items processed before cancellation are reported.
labels.method_text: Each file was opened read-only, hashed in a single pass with the selected algorithms, and checked against a table of file signatures. Every action was written to a hash-chained audit log.
labels.next_ok: No action needed for this file.
labels.next_attention: Review the findings below with your examiner before relying on this file.
labels.next_problem: Do not rely on this file until the examiner has explained the problem.
labels.summary_ok: The file was hashed and checked. The checks applied found no issues.
labels.summary_attention: The file was hashed and checked. Some points need attention.
labels.summary_problem: The file could not be fully examined or shows a serious problem.
labels.fingerprint_text: This fingerprint identifies the exact content of the file. Any change, even of one character, would produce a different value.
labels.timestamp_pending: Pending — the time-stamping service could not be reached; add it later with the timestamp command
labels.not_signed: This PDF is not digitally signed.
labels.case_status_registered: Registered at intake by this run
labels.case_status_verified: Verified: identical to the registered evidence
labels.registered: With an evidence ID from intake

EMPTY_FILE.title: Empty file
EMPTY_FILE.shows: The file contains no data (0 bytes).
EMPTY_FILE.does_not_prove: It does not show whether the file was emptied deliberately or created empty.

EXTENSION_MISMATCH.title: Extension does not match content
EXTENSION_MISMATCH.shows: The name ends in .%{extension} but the content starts with the signature of a %{detected} file.
EXTENSION_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: Renaming is common and often innocent; it does not by itself prove an attempt to hide content.

EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.title: Executable content under another name
EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.shows: The content is a %{detected} program although the name ends in .%{extension}.
EXECUTABLE_CONTENT.does_not_prove: It does not show that the program is malicious; analyse it in an isolated environment.

DUPLICATE.title: Duplicate content
DUPLICATE.does_not_prove: Identical hashes show identical content, not who copied the file or when.

UNREADABLE.title: File could not be read
UNREADABLE.does_not_prove: It does not show that the file is damaged; permissions or locks can cause this.

EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH_WITH_CASE.title: Differs from the evidence registered in the case
EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH_WITH_CASE.shows: The %{algorithm} of this file is %{actual}, but evidence %{evidence_id} was registered at intake with %{expected}: the file examined is not bit-identical to the registered item.
EVIDENCE_HASH_MISMATCH_WITH_CASE.does_not_prove: Who changed the file, when, or whether the change was deliberate; the analysis still ran so the examiner can decide.

EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_CASE_REGISTRY.title: Not registered in the case
EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_CASE_REGISTRY.shows: No item of case %{case_id} was registered with this path or this content, so its continuity from intake cannot be shown.
EVIDENCE_NOT_IN_CASE_REGISTRY.does_not_prove: That the file is altered or irrelevant; it may simply not have gone through intake.

REGISTRY_PATH_CONTENT_CHANGED.title: Registered path now holds different content
REGISTRY_PATH_CONTENT_CHANGED.shows: This path was registered earlier as %{previous_id} with other content; the current content gets a new evidence ID.
REGISTRY_PATH_CONTENT_CHANGED.does_not_prove: Which version is the original or why the content changed.

CERT_CHAIN_VALID.title: Certificate chain valid at the date checked
CERT_CHAIN_VALID.shows: OpenSSL built a path from %{subject} to the trust anchor %{anchor} and every check passed (signatures, validity at %{at}, purpose, constraints and the revocation information supplied).
CERT_CHAIN_VALID.does_not_prove: That the certificate holder signed or approved any particular document, that the anchor deserves trust (that is the examiner's choice of --anchor), or that the result holds at another date.

CERT_CHAIN_UNTRUSTED.title: Chain does not reach a trusted anchor
CERT_CHAIN_UNTRUSTED.shows: No path from %{subject} to any of the anchors given could be completed. OpenSSL reported at depth %{depth}: %{reason} (code %{code}).
CERT_CHAIN_UNTRUSTED.does_not_prove: That the certificate is forged or invalid: the issuing CA may simply not be among the anchors chosen, or an intermediate certificate may be missing from the material examined.

CERT_SIGNATURE_INVALID.title: Certificate signature does not verify
CERT_SIGNATURE_INVALID.shows: The signature on %{subject} (depth %{depth}) does not verify with its issuer's public key: %{reason}.
CERT_SIGNATURE_INVALID.does_not_prove: Who altered the certificate or why; a damaged copy or a certificate attributed to the wrong issuer gives the same result.

CERT_EXPIRED_AT_DATE.title: Certificate expired at the date checked
CERT_EXPIRED_AT_DATE.shows: %{subject} was valid until %{not_after}; the chain was checked at %{at}, after that date.
CERT_EXPIRED_AT_DATE.does_not_prove: That a signature made with it is invalid: what matters for a signature is the validity at signing time (check again with --at signing-time or the date of signing). Expiry of old certificates is normal.

CERT_NOT_YET_VALID_AT_DATE.title: Certificate not yet valid at the date checked
CERT_NOT_YET_VALID_AT_DATE.shows: %{subject} is valid only from %{not_before}; the chain was checked at %{at}, before that date.
CERT_NOT_YET_VALID_AT_DATE.does_not_prove: That the certificate was back-dated or forged; a wrong --at value, a wrong system clock or a signing time recorded in another time zone produce the same result.

CERT_REVOKED.title: Certificate revoked
CERT_REVOKED.shows: %{subject} (serial %{serial}) is listed as revoked since %{revoked_at}, reason %{reason}, according to %{source}.
CERT_REVOKED.does_not_prove: That the holder did anything wrong (revocation also follows routine changes such as a superseded key) or that signatures made before %{revoked_at} are invalid.

REVOCATION_UNKNOWN.title: Revocation status unknown
REVOCATION_UNKNOWN.shows: No CRL or OCSP response covering %{subject} was available for the date checked (%{source}); its revocation status could not be determined.
REVOCATION_UNKNOWN.does_not_prove: That the certificate is revoked or that it is not; supply the CA's CRL or an OCSP response (--crl, --ocsp) to decide.

CERT_PURPOSE_MISMATCH.title: Certificate not issued for this purpose
CERT_PURPOSE_MISMATCH.shows: %{subject} does not allow the purpose %{purpose}: key usage %{key_usage}, extended key usage %{eku}.
CERT_PURPOSE_MISMATCH.does_not_prove: That the certificate was misused on purpose; software often accepts such certificates, and the purpose checked is the one chosen with --purpose.

CERT_NAME_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.title: Name outside the issuing CA's constraints
CERT_NAME_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.shows: The name %{name} in %{subject} is outside the names that %{constraint_by} is allowed to certify (name constraints).
CERT_NAME_CONSTRAINT_VIOLATION.does_not_prove: That the certificate is malicious; it shows only that a CA issued a name it was restricted from issuing, which OpenSSL rejects.

CERT_WEAK_KEY.title: Weak public key
CERT_WEAK_KEY.shows: %{subject} uses a %{algorithm} key of %{size}, below current minimums (RSA 2048 bits, elliptic curves of 256 bits).
CERT_WEAK_KEY.does_not_prove: That the key was broken or that signatures made with it are false; it shows a lower resistance to attack than current practice requires.

CERT_WEAK_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.title: Weak signature algorithm
CERT_WEAK_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.shows: %{subject} is signed with %{algorithm}, a hash algorithm with known collision attacks (MD5, SHA-1).
CERT_WEAK_SIGNATURE_ALGORITHM.does_not_prove: That this certificate was forged; it shows that a collision forgery was feasible for an attacker with the means, so the certificate deserves less weight on its own.

CERT_SELF_SIGNED.title: Self-signed certificate
CERT_SELF_SIGNED.shows: %{subject} is signed by its own key (subject and issuer are identical): it is a root or a stand-alone certificate.
CERT_SELF_SIGNED.does_not_prove: That it is untrustworthy; every root CA is self-signed. Its trust depends only on whether it is one of the anchors chosen.

CERT_IN_TRUST_LIST.title: Issuer listed in a trust list
CERT_IN_TRUST_LIST.shows: %{subject} belongs to the service %{service} listed in %{list} (snapshot %{snapshot}); its status at %{at} was %{status}.
CERT_IN_TRUST_LIST.does_not_prove: That the certificate or signature is qualified or legally valid: that also depends on the service type, the certificate's own statements and the snapshot being current. The list's own signature is not verified in v0.1.

CERT_NOT_IN_TRUST_LIST.title: Not found in the trust list used
CERT_NOT_IN_TRUST_LIST.shows: No certificate of the chain of %{subject} is a service identity of %{list} (snapshot %{snapshot}).
CERT_NOT_IN_TRUST_LIST.does_not_prove: That the certificate is invalid or untrustworthy; most certificates are legitimately outside these lists, and the snapshot may be out of date.

CERT_ISSUED_BY_RAKVOR_INTERNAL.title: Rakvor internal certificate (internal use only)
CERT_ISSUED_BY_RAKVOR_INTERNAL.shows: %{subject} was issued by Rakvor's internal PKI (policy %{policy}). It is for Rakvor's internal use only: it is not a firma digital under Ley 527 de 1999, art. 28 (Colombia), because Rakvor is not an authorised entidad de certificación, and it is not a qualified certificate under eIDAS (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014).
CERT_ISSUED_BY_RAKVOR_INTERNAL.does_not_prove: Any legal effect equivalent to a handwritten signature, and the identity of a signer beyond Rakvor's own internal records; a signature made with it shows only that it was made with a key Rakvor issued.

KEY_MATCHES_CERTIFICATE.title: Private key matches a certificate
KEY_MATCHES_CERTIFICATE.shows: The public part of the private key in %{key} equals the public key of %{certificates}.
KEY_MATCHES_CERTIFICATE.does_not_prove: Who held or used the key, or that the key was not copied elsewhere; the key itself was used only in memory and is not reproduced in any report.

KEY_DOES_NOT_MATCH.title: Private key does not match its certificate
KEY_DOES_NOT_MATCH.shows: The private key in %{key} is not the key of %{certificate}, the certificate supplied with it.
KEY_DOES_NOT_MATCH.does_not_prove: Which key is the right one, or that anything was tampered with; keys and certificates are often mixed up when exported or renewed.

KEY_NOT_PAIRED.title: Private key without a matching certificate
KEY_NOT_PAIRED.shows: No certificate examined in this run has the public key of the private key in %{key}.
KEY_NOT_PAIRED.does_not_prove: That the key is foreign or suspicious; its certificate may simply not be part of the material examined.

TIMESTAMP_TOKEN_VALID.title: Timestamp token valid
TIMESTAMP_TOKEN_VALID.shows: The RFC 3161 token states the time %{gen_time}; its signature by %{tsa} verifies (policy %{policy}, imprint %{hash_algorithm}) and the TSA certificate chain was valid at that time.
TIMESTAMP_TOKEN_VALID.does_not_prove: That the timestamped data is authentic or who submitted it; it proves only that data with this digest existed at that time, as far as the TSA and the anchors chosen are trusted.

TIMESTAMP_TOKEN_INVALID.title: Timestamp token does not verify
TIMESTAMP_TOKEN_INVALID.shows: The RFC 3161 token could not be verified: %{reason}.
TIMESTAMP_TOKEN_INVALID.does_not_prove: That the time it states is false or that the token was forged; a missing TSA certificate, an anchor not supplied or a damaged copy give the same result.

PKCS12_UNREADABLE.title: PKCS#12 file could not be opened
PKCS12_UNREADABLE.shows: The PKCS#12 (PFX) store could not be read: %{reason}. Only what is readable without the password was examined.
PKCS12_UNREADABLE.does_not_prove: That the file is damaged or that its content is suspicious; a missing or wrong password, or a legacy encryption, has the same effect. The password is never recorded.

CRYPTO_INPUT_NOT_RECOGNISED.title: Not a recognised cryptographic object
CRYPTO_INPUT_NOT_RECOGNISED.shows: The content is not a certificate, certificate bundle, PKCS#7, PKCS#12, CRL, OCSP response, timestamp token, private key or CSR (%{kind}); only the general file checks were applied.
CRYPTO_INPUT_NOT_RECOGNISED.does_not_prove: That the file is irrelevant or harmless; it was simply not analysed as cryptographic evidence.

CRYPTO_INPUT_UNPARSABLE.title: Cryptographic object could not be parsed
CRYPTO_INPUT_UNPARSABLE.shows: The content looks like a %{kind} but could not be decoded: %{error}.
CRYPTO_INPUT_UNPARSABLE.does_not_prove: That it was tampered with; truncation during copy, an unusual encoding or a format this version does not support give the same result.

ANALYSIS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.title: Analysis step not available in this build
ANALYSIS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.shows: The step %{operation} is not implemented in this development build, so the item was hashed and registered but not analysed as cryptographic evidence.
ANALYSIS_NOT_IMPLEMENTED.does_not_prove: Anything about the item's certificates, keys or signatures; run a release build before relying on this report.

EVIDENCE_CHANGED_DURING_READ.title: File changed while it was being examined
EVIDENCE_CHANGED_DURING_READ.shows: The bytes analysed have %{algorithm} %{actual}, but the same file hashed %{expected} moments before: the file changed during the examination.
EVIDENCE_CHANGED_DURING_READ.does_not_prove: Who or what changed it (another program, synchronisation, failing media); the analysis results may not describe the registered item.

ANALYSIS_STEP_FAILED.title: Analysis step failed
ANALYSIS_STEP_FAILED.shows: The step %{operation} stopped with an error: %{error}. The other results for this item remain valid, but this step gave no answer.
ANALYSIS_STEP_FAILED.does_not_prove: Anything about what the step would have found; repeat it after correcting the cause (missing anchor file, unsupported format...).

limitations.SIGNATURE_TABLE_LIMITED: Type detection uses a limited table of common file signatures; unknown types are reported as unknown, not as suspicious.
limitations.TIMESTAMPS_FROM_FILESYSTEM: Modification times come from the file system of the examined copy and may differ from the original source.
limitations.CLEAN_RESULT_IS_NOT_AUTHENTICITY: A result without findings does not prove that a file is authentic or unaltered before acquisition.
limitations.TIMESTAMP_PROVES_EXISTENCE_ONLY: A trusted timestamp proves the audit log existed in this exact form at the stated time; it does not prove that the examined copy matches the original source.
limitations.VALIDATION_IS_AS_OF_THE_DATE_GIVEN: Every chain is judged at one instant (--at, recorded in each report); the same certificate can be valid at one date and expired or revoked at another.
limitations.OFFLINE_REVOCATION_DEPENDS_ON_SUPPLIED_F: Offline, revocation is checked only against the CRLs and OCSP responses supplied (--crl, --ocsp, or found among the evidence); a revocation published elsewhere is not seen.
limitations.TRUST_LIST_SNAPSHOT_DATED: Trust lists are used as dated snapshots (date and SHA-256 recorded); services added, suspended or withdrawn after the snapshot are not reflected.
limitations.TRUST_LIST_SIGNATURE_NOT_VERIFIED_V01: In version 0.1 the trust list's own XAdES signature is not verified; the snapshot's source and SHA-256 are recorded so it can be checked independently. The Colombian list is a curated file, because ONAC publishes no machine-readable list.
limitations.RAKVOR_CERTIFICATES_ARE_INTERNAL_USE: Certificates issued by Rakvor's internal PKI are for internal use only: they are not a firma digital under Ley 527 de 1999, art. 28 (Colombia), and not qualified certificates under eIDAS (Regulation (EU) No 910/2014).
limitations.NO_VALIDATED_ERROR_RATES_YET: The tool's results have been compared with OpenSSL and Python reference implementations on test sets, but no error rate has yet been measured on a validated corpus.

custody.title_fr: Chain of custody sheet — digital evidence (France)
custody.basis_co: Prepared following Law 906 of 2004 (arts. 254–266), the chain-of-custody manual of the Attorney General's Office (Fiscalía) and Law 527 of 1999.
custody.basis_fr: Prepared for an expert examination under the French Code of Criminal Procedure (arts. 156 ff.); the seal number refers to the judicial seal (scellé).
custody.operation_text: Read-only hashing and analysis by %{tool} %{version}, run %{run_id}, from %{start} to %{end} (UTC). Audit entries #%{first}–#%{last}.

ui.audit_note: Every action is written to a tamper-evident audit log.
ui.evidence_help: Add one file, several files or whole folders (bulk review). You can also drag them onto this window.
ui.path_hint: …or type / paste a path and press Enter
ui.hash_tip_two: Two algorithms are already selected: untick one first.
ui.hash_tip_one: At least one algorithm is required.

ui.no_anchor_warning: No anchor: every chain is reported as untrusted.
ui.online_box: Fetch CRLs and OCSP from the certificates' URLs
ui.online_warning: Goes on the network. Every fetch (URL, time, response SHA-256) is written to the audit log and chain.json.
ui.p12_password_note: Opens .p12/.pfx items and encrypted keys. Used for one run, then wiped; never logged.
ui.results_empty: Run an analysis: one row per item appears here.
ui.select_item: Select a row to see its chain.
ui.no_chain: No certificate chain for this item.
ui.verify_ok: issued.jsonl chain intact, every recorded file matches
ui.runs_folder_note: Every operation writes <folder>/logs/<RUN-ID>/audit.jsonl and <folder>/reports/<RUN-ID>/report.txt, as the CLI does.
ui.module_hint: PKCS#11 module, e.g. C:\Program Files\Yubico\Yubico PIV Tool\bin\libykcs11.dll
ui.wizards: What do you want to create?
ui.wz_new_root_help: Creates an offline root CA in an empty folder (pki init-root). Put the key on a token for the real root.
ui.wz_import_help: Brings an existing CA certificate and its key under management (pki import), e.g. the intermediate just issued.
ui.wz_issue_help: Issues one certificate from the opened CA folder (pki issue).
ui.wz_revoke_help: Marks an issued certificate revoked (pki revoke); publish it with a new CRL.
ui.wz_crl_help: Signs a CRL with every revoked serial (pki crl): crl/<n>.crl and crl/latest.crl.
ui.wz_csr_help: Creates a key and a PKCS#10 request for a public or qualified CA (csr new).
ui.wz_lab_help: Writes a reproducible lab set and its expected_findings.json (lab make).
ui.internal_notice: Internal use only: not a firma digital (Ley 527 de 1999 art. 28), not qualified under eIDAS.
